short: A peace treaty between Sweden and Denmark-Norway that temporarily knocked Denmark out of the Great Northern War.
full:
Signed on 18 August 1700, the Treaty of Traventhal forced Denmark-Norway to exit the anti-Swedish coalition early in the Great Northern War. Following a rapid and successful Swedish landing on Zealand near Copenhagen led by Charles XII, King Frederick IV of Denmark sued for peace to save his capital.

Denmark acknowledged the independence of Holstein-Gottorp and agreed to pay an indemnity, promising not to engage in further hostilities against Sweden. This rapid victory allowed Charles XII to shift his focus entirely to the Russian and Saxon-Polish threats, keeping Denmark out of the war for the next nine years.
